chunks: “Among what Musa ibn 'Imran عليه السلام privately spoke with his Lord, Mighty and Glorious, was that he said: ‘O Lord, what reward has been attained for visiting the sick?’ He said: ‘I appoint for him an angel who visits him in his grave until his gathering place.’ He said: ‘O Lord, then what is for the one who washes the dead?’ He said: ‘I wash him of his sins like the day his mother gave birth to him.’”

key_terms.إِلَى مَحْشَرِهِ: until his resurrection and gathering for judgment
key_terms.الْأَجْرِ: the divine reward granted for a righteous act
key_terms.عِيَادَةِ الْمَرِيضِ: visiting and caring for a sick person
key_terms.غَسَّلَ الْمَوْتَى: performed the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.فِي قَبْرِهِ: in his grave, referring to the state after death
key_terms.كَيَوْمِ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ: like the day his mother gave birth to him, meaning complete cleansing from sins

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the sick and washing the deceased in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the great reward for acts of mercy toward the sick and the deceased. It teaches that visiting the sick brings ongoing care in the grave, while washing the dead becomes a means of purification from sins.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.387 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:

"In what Musa ibn Imran (as) privately spoke to his Lord (azj), the Mighty and Glorious,
Musa (as) said: 'O’ Lord (azj), what is the reward for visiting the sick?'
Allah (swt) replied: 'I will appoint an angel to visit them in their grave until the Day of Resurrection.'
Musa (as) asked: 'O’ Lord (azj), what about the one who washes the deceased?'
Allah (swt) replied: 'I will cleanse them of their sins as on the day their mother gave birth to them.'"
